Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 70, verses 1–4:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Ma'arij (the Ascending Stairways), because it mentions the ascent of the angels and the Spirit (al-Ruh) from the earth to the heavens at the beginning of the surah.

Some of the surah's objectives

• Warning the disbelievers of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, depicting their state on that dreadful day, and affirming and consoling the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding what he endures from the mocking polytheists.

• Mention of human nature: its impatience (jaza') in times of hardship, its arrogance (bata') in times of blessing, and the contrast of this with the deeds of the believers that earned them the abode of honor.

• Emphasis, by oath, that resurrection and recompense are a truth beyond doubt.

[The Tafsir]

A caller from among the polytheists invoked upon himself and his people the descent of punishment upon them. It will certainly befall them on the Day of Resurrection, and none can prevent it from Allah, the Lord of the Ascents and Majesty. The angels and Gabriel ascend to Him, may He be exalted, on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years of worldly years, and for the believer it is like an obligatory prayer.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 70, verses 19–30:

Indeed, man was created with a tendency toward anxiety and intense greed. When misfortune and hardship befall him, he is excessively distressed and grieved; and when good and ease come to him, he is excessively withholding and tight-fisted. Except for those who observe prayer (al-salah), who keep to performing it at all its times, and whom nothing distracts from it; and those in whose wealth there is a specified portion that Allah has made obligatory upon them, namely zakat (obligatory almsgiving), for the one who asks them for help, and for the one who refrains from asking for it; and those who believe in the Day of Reckoning and recompense, and so prepare for it with righteous deeds; and those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord. Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something anyone should feel secure from. And those who guard their private parts from everything Allah has forbidden them, except with their spouses and their female slaves, for then they are not blameworthy.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 70, verses 31–35:

Whoever seeks beyond that (to satisfy his desire), other than wives and those his right hand possesses, then those are the transgressors, having passed from the lawful to the unlawful. And those who are guardians of the trusts of Allah and the trusts of the people, and who keep their covenants with Allah and with the people, and those who give their testimonies with truth, without alteration or concealment, and those who maintain their prayer and do not neglect any of its obligations. Those who are characterized by these sublime attributes will abide in Gardens of Bliss, honored therein with every kind of honor.

Does every one of these disbelievers hope that Allah will admit him into the Garden of everlasting bliss? The matter is not as they hope, for they will never enter it. Indeed, We created them from what they know, from a despised fluid, just like others, yet they did not believe. So how do they expect the honor of entering the Garden of bliss?

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 70, verse 40:

Exalted is He, who swore by Himself, and He is the Lord of the easts and the wests, by the sun, the moon, and the rest of the stars, because in them are the striking signs that point to the Resurrection: that We are certainly able to do so with complete power.
"We are able to replace them with a people better than them and more obedient to God, and no one can outrun Us or escape Us or prevent Us if We wish to bring other people better than them."

But it has already been decreed in Our knowledge and Our will that the punishment of these disbelievers be delayed, and that they not be replaced by other people. So leave them to plunge into their falsehood and to play in their worldly life, until they encounter the Day of Resurgence (yawm al-qiyamah) in which they are promised punishment; the Day on which they will come out of the graves hastening, just as they used to hasten in the world to their gods that they had invented for worship besides Allah. They will rush and hurry, their gazes humbled and lowered to the ground, overcome by abasement and humiliation. That is the Day they were promised in the world, and they used to mock it and deny it.
